title: Layoff Survival Calculator
description: Calculate your financial runway and determine how long you can survive without a regular paycheck.
methodSummary: Monthly spending = expenses + debt payments, counted once.
During benefit payments, savings fall by spending minus monthly benefits.
If savings run out before benefits end, runway stops there. Otherwise, remaining cash funds spending after benefits end.
assumptions: Savings and net severance are available now.
Benefits begin immediately and last for the entered duration; use zero if uncertain.
Spending is constant. The model is a monthly approximation, not a daily payment schedule.
insights: Future benefit payments cannot cover a cash shortfall today.
Try a no-benefits scenario and include new insurance costs in spending.

richContent:
Why payment timing changes runway

With $1,000 in savings, $3,000 monthly spending and $1,000 monthly benefits, cash falls by $2,000 a month. It runs out after about half a month even if benefits were approved for six months. Adding all six future payments to savings would incorrectly report 2.3 months.

With $12,000 in savings and the same spending and benefits, the savings cover the $2,000 monthly shortfall for six months. Compare both examples with your own payment calendar. A monthly average can miss a rent bill due before a benefit payment.

Build the spending estimate

Include housing, food, utilities, insurance, transport and required debt payments. Keep tax reserves and one-time bills separate. The career transition checklist explains how to stress-test the budget.
quickAnswer: Runway depends on when benefits arrive as well as their total amount. Enter available cash, monthly spending, and the duration of confirmed benefits.
resultNote: Assumes benefits start immediately and arrive evenly. Payment delays, unexpected bills and benefit eligibility are not modeled. Six months is an example reserve, not a guarantee of safety.
